correctness.rationale: The two row-column graphs are cubic for n>=3. The exhaustive 3-colour successor list (y,x),(y,z),(z,x) is forced by properness. A swapped step contradicts the distinct-coloured rung at the next step; a non-swapped step forces a rigid three-cycle preserving orientation. This proves impossibility of twisted closure and exactly 12 named 3-colour prism solutions when 3 divides n. All four-colour residue-class prescriptions were re-derived from the boundary rule and checked directly at the seam and tail; both infinite lower bounds and upper constructions are self-contained. A standalone 18-state/12-transition enumerator, 1196 explicit witness tests n<=600, and 26 exhaustive named-solution counts n<=15 all pass. Finite checks corroborate but do not replace proof.

originality.rationale: Exact three-colour two-dynamic numbers and colorings for cyclic/twisted cubic ladders are not supplied by the October 2026 paper: it treats claw-free cubic square colouring and a 4-regular circulant different from the present ladders. The 2003 global subcubic upper bound implies \(\chi_2\le4\), so that upper bound is expressly credited and not claimed independently. The 2013 perfect/equitable colouring classification restricts neighbourhood colour multiplicities uniformly within each class; a 2-dynamic 3-colouring need not be equitable (indeed the constructed prism witnesses have colour-class-dependent vertex neighbourhood multiplicities), hence the source does not directly imply the absence of all non-equitable solutions. The 2026 proper chromatic-polynomial transfer matrix studies all proper colourings and does not isolate the local surjectivity constraint. Semantic published-record queries and comparison to accessible earlier colouring claims found no overlapping dynamic-ladder theorem. Unavailable 2013 full text and possible unindexed fall-colouring literature are residual risks, not treated as uniqueness certification.

value.rationale: The period-three handedness theorem is a structural local constraint, not the known subcubic upper bound or a standard proper-colouring fact. It explains a topology-sensitive obstruction: for every multiple-of-three circumference, the orientable prism has exactly twelve named optimal three-colour patterns but the locally identical Möbius ladder has none. Exact sharp infinite-family classification and optimal-colouring enumeration are mathematically motivated by the dynamic-colouring hierarchy and provide a reusable twisted-boundary test; not an arbitrary parameter slice.
